title: Crypto.com and TMTG
summary: Each core fact is documented. Crypto.com agreed on 2025-08-26 to take $50M of TMTG stock as part of a CRO-treasury deal, and that swap closed on 2025-09-05 (TMTG paid for $105M of CRO half in its own shares); the larger SPAC treasury plan was terminated on 2026-08-07. The SEC closed its Crypto.com probe with no action on 2025-03-27. Crypto.com gave about $36M ($35M to MAGA Inc. plus $1M to the inauguration). The CFTC filed an amicus brief for Crypto.com on 2026-02-17, and the OCC conditionally approved its trust charter on 2026-02-23. The video errs in calling Crypto.com the party 'facing' the lawsuit: it was the plaintiff, and it lost at the Ninth Circuit. Beyond timing, no quid pro quo is documented, and Crypto.com denies any link.

sub_claims.statement: Crypto.com agreed to purchase $50M in TMTG stock in a strategic partnership.
sub_claims.finding: Announced 2025-08-26 with the formation of Trump Media Group CRO Strategy, a treasury company to be listed through a merger with Yorkville Acquisition Corp (ticker MCGA). Audit correction: the bilateral part closed on 2025-09-05 (The Block, Blockworks). TMTG acquired 684.4M CRO (about $105M at about $0.153), paid 50/50 in cash and TMTG stock. Crypto.com therefore received about $50M of DJT shares (about 2.8M shares per one report), both sides locked up. It was a stock-for-token swap, not a cash purchase of stock. The separate CRO Strategy SPAC treasury plan was never completed. TMTG, Crypto.com and Yorkville mutually terminated it on 2026-08-07, citing market conditions, and also dropped the Yorkville ETF servicing deal and the direct Truth Social prediction-market integration, replacing the latter with a marketing deal.

sub_claims.statement: The partnership came months after the SEC closed its investigation into Crypto.com with no action.
sub_claims.finding: The SEC closed the probe with no action on 2025-03-27, after an August 2024 Wells notice. The $50M deal came about five months later. However, the first TMTG/Crypto.com partnership (Truth.Fi ETFs) was announced on 2025-03-24, three days before the closure.

sub_claims.statement: This followed Trump nominating a new pro-crypto SEC commissioner.
sub_claims.finding: Trump named the crypto-friendly Paul Atkins as SEC Chair in December 2024 and Mark Uyeda as acting chair in January 2025, both before the probe closed. I found no separate 2026 commissioner nomination.

sub_claims.statement: Crypto.com spent $36M on contributions to Trump and Trump-affiliated PACs.
sub_claims.finding: Molly White's tracker lists $36M (campaign, inauguration, pro-Trump PACs since 2024). The pieces: $1M to the inauguration and $10M to MAGA Inc. in February 2025 (AP); two more $10M gifts from Foris DAX in Sep-Oct 2025 and $5M in January 2026 (FEC filings via Decrypt and KuCoin). That is about $35M to MAGA Inc. plus $1M, nearly all to one super PAC.

sub_claims.statement: The CFTC filed an amicus brief in favor of Crypto.com in a prediction-markets lawsuit Crypto.com was facing.
sub_claims.finding: The CFTC under Mike Selig filed the brief on 2026-02-17 in the Ninth Circuit (No. 25-7187), arguing that event contracts are swaps under exclusive CFTC jurisdiction. But Crypto.com Derivatives North America was the plaintiff: it sued the Nevada Gaming Control Board in June 2025. It lost its preliminary injunction bid in October 2025 and lost at the Ninth Circuit on 2026-08-28. A cert petition (No. 26-344) was filed in September 2026.

sub_claims.statement: Crypto.com's national trust bank charter application was provisionally approved.
sub_claims.finding: Crypto.com applied in October 2025. On 2026-02-23 the OCC granted conditional approval for Foris DAX National Trust Bank, covering custody, staking and settlement, with no deposits or loans. Final approval depends on pre-opening conditions, and I found no report of final approval.

corrections: Transcript says Crypto.com was 'facing' a prediction-markets lawsuit. Crypto.com (through CDNA) was the plaintiff suing Nevada regulators, and it lost at the Ninth Circuit on 2026-08-28 despite the CFTC brief.
Transcript says $36M went to 'Trump affiliated PACs'. The figure is Molly White's tally: about $35M to MAGA Inc. plus $1M to the inauguration.
The 'new pro-crypto SEC commissioner' was Paul Atkins, named Chair in December 2024, before the probe closed.
The first Crypto.com/TMTG partnership (ETFs) was announced 2025-03-24, three days before the SEC closure, not months after.
Transcript says the charter was 'provisionally approved'. The OCC's approval is conditional, and final approval is pending.

The $50M of TMTG stock did change hands: on 2025-09-05 TMTG paid for 684.4M CRO (about $105M) half in cash and half in its own stock. Crypto.com received the shares as payment for tokens, not through a cash purchase. The larger CRO Strategy SPAC treasury plan was terminated on 2026-08-07.
denials_and_context: A Crypto.com spokeswoman told AP there is 'absolutely no connection' between the SEC decision and its political activity. TMTG called AP's story politically driven.
The White House (Karoline Leavitt) denies that the President or his family engage in conflicts of interest.

The SEC dropped or closed almost all Gensler-era crypto exchange cases in early 2025 (Coinbase, Kraken, Robinhood, Uniswap and others), and the Cumberland DRW case was dismissed the same day. Crypto.com's closure fits that broad pattern.
The CFTC's jurisdictional position helps all prediction-market operators (for example Kalshi), not only Crypto.com. Other crypto firms received similar OCC conditional charters in the same period.
Cutting the other way: Crypto.com is MAGA Inc.'s largest donor, and its CDNA exchange powers TMTG's own Truth Predict product, so the CFTC brief also indirectly supports a Trump-owned business.

changes: Corrected sub-claim 1, the summary and the corrections. The write-up said there was no confirmation that the $50M stock purchase closed, but The Block and Blockworks report the swap closed on 2025-09-05: TMTG paid for 684.4M CRO (about $105M) half in cash and half in DJT stock, so Crypto.com received about $50M of TMTG shares.
Added the 2026-08-07 mutual termination of the Trump Media Group CRO Strategy SPAC plan (The Block, Axios), with relationship edges.
